stories.title: Kill The Cookie Banner
stories.blurb: A European initiative pushing to legally eliminate the ubiquitous cookie consent banner plague. With 522 comments and over 1000 upvotes, HN clearly has feelings about this. If you've ever rage-clicked 'Accept All' just to read an article, this one's for you.

stories.title: US citizen charged after GrapheneOS phone wipes during airport search
stories.blurb: A US citizen faces charges after his GrapheneOS device auto-wiped during a border search — and prosecutors are treating the wipe itself as suspicious. A chilling case study in the legal risks of privacy-first mobile choices, and the most-discussed story on HN today.

stories.title: PGSimCity - How PostgreSQL Works
stories.blurb: A gorgeous SimCity-style interactive visualization that explains PostgreSQL internals — vacuum, WAL, autovacuum, and more. If you've ever wanted to understand what Postgres is actually doing under the hood, this is the most fun way to learn it.

stories.title: Kimi-K3 Releases on HuggingFace 7/27
stories.blurb: Moonshot AI drops Kimi-K3 on HuggingFace today — another frontier-class open-weights model entering the race. Early benchmarks in the thread are drawing comparisons to top-tier models. Worth grabbing if you're evaluating alternatives to Claude or GPT for coding workflows.

stories.title: The New AI Superpowers: Focus and Followthrough
stories.blurb: A thoughtful take on what actually differentiates effective AI-assisted developers from the rest — it's not prompting tricks, it's human discipline around focus and follow-through. Directly relevant if you're using Claude Code and wondering why some days feel more productive than others.

stories.title: Scriptc by Vercel: TypeScript-to-Native compiler, no JavaScript engine in binary
stories.blurb: Vercel's experimental compiler turns TypeScript directly into native binaries with zero JavaScript runtime dependency. For a TypeScript/.NET developer, this is a compelling peek at a future where TS isn't just a transpile-to-JS story. The HN thread has healthy skepticism worth reading.

stories.title: Decker, a platform that builds on the legacy of Hypercard and classic macOS
stories.blurb: Decker is a modern revival of HyperCard's card-and-stack paradigm, deeply influenced by classic Mac aesthetics and philosophy. It's a creative coding / rapid prototyping tool that feels like nothing else out there — instantly appealing to anyone who misses the Mac of the early '90s.

stories.title: Design is compromise
stories.blurb: Steph Ango — the founder of Obsidian — writes about why every design decision is a tradeoff and why that's not a weakness but a feature. Given the author, this is practically a behind-the-scenes philosophy piece for one of the reader's core tools.

stories.title: We have proof automation now
stories.blurb: Adam Langley (of BoringSSL fame) describes using AI-assisted formal proof tools to verify a zstd implementation in Lean. It's a landmark moment: proof automation has crossed a threshold where real-world cryptographic code can be formally verified at reasonable cost.

stories.title: French firefighters face 'pyrocumulonimbus' for first time
stories.blurb: Pyrocumulonimbus clouds — fire-generated thunderstorms that can create their own lightning and spread fires unpredictably — appeared in France for the first time ever. Climate scientists have warned about this phenomenon for years; now it's arrived in Western Europe.

stories.title: Show HN: Physically accurate black hole you can put in your room
stories.blurb: An AR/web experience that renders a physically accurate, general-relativity-correct black hole and lets you place it in your physical space. The gravitational lensing and photon sphere are rendered in real time. Genuinely jaw-dropping and technically impressive.

stories.title: Simulate cassette tape audio profiles using FFmpeg
stories.blurb: A FFmpeg filter chain that simulates the frequency response, wow-and-flutter, and noise profiles of real cassette tape formats (Type I, II, IV). It's immediately actionable — grab the command and run it on any audio file today for that warm, degraded lo-fi aesthetic.

stories.title: Go Analysis Framework: modular static analysis by go team
stories.blurb: The Go team's official framework for building modular static analysis passes is getting renewed attention. A well-structured walkthrough of how to write your own linters and analyzers using the same infrastructure that powers go vet and staticcheck.

stories.title: The relay market powering token resellers and fraud
stories.blurb: A deep dive into the shadowy ecosystem of LLM API token resellers — who buys stolen API keys, how relay markets operate, and what fraud-at-scale looks like when AI inference is the commodity. Essential reading if you deploy or manage any AI API credentials.

stories.title: Show HN: CheapSecurity – Lightweight, Self-Hosted CCTV for Linux SBCs
stories.blurb: A lean, self-hosted CCTV system designed for Raspberry Pi and similar single-board computers — no cloud, no subscriptions, no data leaving your home. If you care about home security without surrendering footage to a third party, this is worth a look today.

stories.title: Htmx 4.0, the first JavaScript library to release exclusively on the Game Boy
stories.blurb: The htmx team continues its tradition of chaotic, brilliant marketing: version 4.0 ships as a Game Boy cartridge. It's a stunt, but the HN thread has genuine discussion about htmx's technical direction. The merch is real and the vibes are immaculate.

stories.title: I learned PCB design, 3D printing and C just to listen to music
stories.blurb: A developer built a custom hardware music player from scratch — designing PCBs, printing enclosures, and writing firmware in C — purely because no existing device did exactly what they wanted. An inspiring maker story about following a creative itch all the way down the rabbit hole.

stories.title: Introduction to Data-Oriented Design [pdf]
stories.blurb: A classic game-dev PDF on Data-Oriented Design resurfaces on HN with fresh eyes. The core ideas — designing around data layout and cache efficiency rather than object hierarchies — are increasingly relevant as developers wrestle with performance in modern systems.

stories.title: Fonts In Use – Find out where a font is used
stories.blurb: Fonts In Use is a curated archive that documents typefaces used in the wild — posters, books, signage, UI — with credits and context. An invaluable reference for anyone doing design work who wants to identify or find inspiration from real-world typography.

stories.title: I wanted a clock that never needed setting. Things escalated
stories.blurb: An Ars Technica writer's quest for a perfectly self-setting clock spirals into GPS disciplined oscillators, atomic time sources, and DIY timekeeping rabbit holes. It's the kind of delightful hardware obsession that makes the internet worth having.
